chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, both from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about that from which a pigeon drinks, and he said: “Everything whose meat is eaten, wudu (ablution) may be performed from its leftover water, and it may be drunk.” And about water from which a hawk, falcon, or eagle drinks, he said: “From everything among the birds, wudu (ablution) may be performed from what it drinks from, unless you see blood in its beak. So if you see blood in its beak, then do not perform wudu (ablution) from it and do not drink.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Waters, when they are in restricted vessels and an impurity falls into them, wudu (ablution) is not performed from them, and pouring them out becomes obligatory. This is indicated by what we have previously mentioned: that whenever water is less than a kurr, it becomes impure by the impurities that enter it; and when its impurity is established, its use is not permissible without disagreement. This is also indicated by it.

key_terms.الْكُرِّ: the threshold measure of water relevant to impurity rulings
key_terms.دَمًا: blood, whose presence indicates possible impurity here
key_terms.سُؤْرِهِ: the leftover water remaining after an animal has drunk from it
key_terms.نَجَاسَةٌ: ritual impurity falling into the water
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: it may be used for wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with water from which birds have drunk?
ai.summary: This hadith gives rulings on the leftover water of birds and distinguishes between cases of purity and impurity. Water drunk by birds may generally be used for wudu (ablution) and drinking, but if blood is seen on the bird’s beak, it is not to be used; the accompanying statement of al-Shaykh further affirms that confined water becomes impure when najasah falls into it if it is less than kurr.
